correctness.rationale: Holomorphic orders at zero agree by comparing exponential moduli. The first unmatched coefficient produces a nonzero cosine harmonic; irrational rotations have dense phases and rational rotations force two independent real conditions for differences of order below the denominator. The degree-q resonance gives the sharp counterexample. The phase-lift node equality is equivalent to a difference divisible by q; the (d+1)^2-node Vandermonde determinant is nonzero iff d<q. Hermitian dimension proves only the stated linear-lifting lower bound. Critical determinant and finite resonance examples were checked by verify_spiral.py (335 assertions).

value.rationale: The geometry is not an arbitrary finite slice: all samples are iterates of one contraction-rotation, a natural sparse exact-data sampling design. The result provides complete rational/irrational and sharp finite-degree capacity classification, explicit counterexamples at every failing denominator, and a deterministic (d+1)^2-evaluation reconstruction scheme with an exact linear-lift lower bound. Nonlinear minimality and stable recovery are expressly excluded.
